newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists remain bullish on AEX.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists remain bullish on AEX.

text.p: Dutch chartists remain broadly bullish over the prospects of the AEX blue chip share index despite the highs reached already. No resistance levels were given by Rabo Securities and Jaad as the AEX seems to be moving into uncharted territory.
Only MeesPierson is cautious, saying a correction would be healthy.

The AEX index ended at 846.09 points on Friday, 21.66 points above the previous Friday. It was the seventh record close in the last ten trading days. The AEX has gained over 30 percent since the beginning of this year.

MeesPierson's opinion on the long-term trend: Up.
Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.

ING Barings - The uptrend has been boosted following the recent string of new highs. Rising momentum confirms strong near term technicals. Money flow is picking up, but not yet very convincing. This confirms slow inflow of new funds. The advance/decline line remains extremely bullish, suggesting strong leadership in the market.
Another positive sign is the ratio of new 12-month highs. Last week, 110 stocks recorded 12-month highs, against only five with 12-month lows.
The 12-day average of the call-put ratio is at overheated values, signalling active speculative buying.
All in all, we remain positive as most of our indicators favour a bullish scenario. A break below first support at 835 is required to delay positive scope. We hold to our medium target around 875.

MeesPierson - Markets remains strong but a small correction would be healthy. Due to uncertainty around the Amsterdam summit this week, we expect a small dip to the 820 level, where we find a support level of the upgoing trading range.
We still advise investors to use every dip to buy Dutch shares.

Rabo Securities - The index is pushing against a rising resistance line which caps the upward potential for the short-term. Our price target remains 860. We expect a continuation of the current rally unless the rising support line -- currently at 815 -- is broken downwardly.
ABN AMRO - This is still a long market. We expect some hesitation around 850-860. Don't focus on the short side, but buy on weakness. Maintain an exit stop at 841.50.
